name: Keln
summary: Keln Inc. inference platform plus isolated Linux microVM sandboxes and a hosted MCP at mcp.keln.ai/mcp. Prepaid credits; sandboxes billed per second while running.
description: Vendor-affiliated listing (Keln Inc.). Keln is a hosted inference platform for open-weight models at https://keln.ai/ (HTTP 200), with isolated Linux sandboxes and a remote MCP server. Terms of Use (https://keln.ai/terms, HTTP 200, last updated November 11, 2026) are a binding agreement with Keln Inc.; you must be at least 18 and capable of forming a binding contract in your jurisdiction. The Services include the inference API, sandboxes ("isolated environments that run code you or your agents send"), and optional web search. Model requests are served by independent compute providers that Keln selects; Keln remains the sole counterparty. Sandboxes (https://docs.keln.ai/sandboxes/, HTTP 200) each run in their own microVM, not on the operator's machine. The Sandbox API is https://sandbox.keln.ai and uses the same API keys and prepaid balance as inference. Default template `base` is 2 vCPU, 2,048 MiB memory, 10,240 MiB disk, with Python 3, Node.js, git, curl and a C toolchain. Official pricing: $0.0504 per vCPU-hour, $0.0162 per GiB-hour, stored images $0.08 per GB-month; no monthly fee; billed per second while `running` (at least 1 second); `starting` and `paused` time, and paused snapshots, are not billed. A 2 vCPU, 2 GiB default is listed at $0.133 per hour. Default timeout 300 seconds (5 minutes); a sandbox can run at most 24 hours from created_at or the last resume. Creating or resuming requires the balance to cover the first 5 minutes or the API returns 402 insufficient_balance. If the balance runs out while sandboxes are running, Keln stops them after 60 seconds. Official Limits on the sandbox overview (https://docs.keln.ai/sandboxes/, fetched 2026-11-25) list 100 running sandboxes, or 3 before the first paid top-up, per workspace (`429 concurrency_limit`). The same official table lists 100 paused sandboxes, each kept 30 days at most (`429 paused_limit`), and 20 images in `creating` or `ready` (`429 image_limit`). Billing (https://docs.keln.ai/platform/billing/, HTTP 200): workspaces are prepaid; top-ups are by card, $5 to $5,000, with a processing fee of 2.9% + $0.30 itemized at checkout (the fee never comes out of the balance); Stripe handles payment details. Credits pay for Keln usage only, never expire, and are non-refundable except where the law requires it. A request that fails on Keln's side bills nothing; a cancelled generation bills what was delivered. There is no overage billing; at zero the API returns 402. Terms repeat that prepaid credits already paid are non-refundable except where required by law; prices may change prospectively. Disputes: 30-day informal email to contact@keln.ai, then binding AAA arbitration seated in San Francisco County, California, with a class-action waiver. Governing law: State of California, without conflict-of-laws rules; residual court jurisdiction in San Francisco County, California. Hosted MCP at https://mcp.keln.ai/mcp (Streamable HTTP). The sandbox overview itself links to the MCP docs (`../mcp.md`, "Give an AI assistant sandboxes and web search as tools") but does not name the hosted hostname. The dedicated MCP docs page (https://docs.keln.ai/mcp/, re-fetched 2026-11-25, HTTP 200, title "MCP server - Keln Docs") still exists and documents a hosted Streamable HTTP server at https://mcp.keln.ai/mcp: authenticate by signing in with a Keln account in supported apps, or with Authorization: Bearer and a Keln API key; tool calls use standard sandbox and web API pricing with no additional MCP fee. Documented tools include create/list/get/pause/resume/delete sandbox, run_command, file tools, open_port, web_search and web_fetch. Acceptable use for sandboxes (https://docs.keln.ai/sandboxes/acceptable-use/, HTTP 200, supplementing the Terms) prohibits cryptocurrency mining, scanning, spam, and anonymizing proxies; outbound port 25 is blocked. You are responsible for everything that runs in a sandbox, including agent-generated code. Zero data retention on the inference API does not cover sandboxes, which retain files, memory and processes so code can run and resume (data-handling docs). MCP docs: the MCP server doesn't store API keys or retain tool inputs and outputs; it temporarily caches key validation results and addresses that submit invalid keys. No API key, signup, or spend was used, and tools were not called.

agent_access.notes: Bare GET of https://mcp.keln.ai/mcp (and GET with Accept: application/json or text/event-stream) returned HTTP 401 application/json {"error":"invalid_token","message":"Send your Keln API key as Authorization: Bearer <key>."} with WWW-Authenticate Bearer realm="keln", resource_metadata="https://mcp.keln.ai/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp". Unauthenticated initialize and tools/list POSTs returned the same 401. That well-known document (HTTP 200) lists resource https://mcp.keln.ai/mcp, authorization_servers https://auth.keln.ai, and scopes_supported openid, email, profile, offline_access. Tools were not called; no API key, signup, or spend. Official docs: Streamable HTTP; sign-in or Bearer API key; no additional MCP fee. Sandboxes run on Keln microVMs, not the operator's machine.
